visualTexts.title: Sports Day Helpers Wanted
visualTexts.html:
SPORTS DAY — HELPERS WANTED

Sports Day is on Saturday, 8 November. Primary 3 pupils may sign up for one job only. Ask your form teacher for a form.

JobWhereTimeHelpers needed
Handing out waterField gate8.00 – 10.00 a.m.6
Collecting score cardsTeachers' table8.30 – 11.00 a.m.4
Minding the lost property boxHall foyer8.00 a.m. – 12 noon2
Tidying the equipment storeBehind the hall11.00 a.m. – 12 noon8

Every helper gets a free drink and a badge. Wear your PE shirt. Sign up by Friday, 31 October.

questions.q: On what date is Sports Day?
questions.tip: The first line of the notice gives the date.

questions.q: How many pupils are needed to tidy the equipment store?
questions.tip: Read across the last row to the 'Helpers needed' column.

questions.q: Which job starts at 8.30 a.m.?
questions.tip: Look down the 'Time' column for 8.30.

questions.q: Which job lasts the longest?
questions.tip: Work out how many hours each job lasts. One runs from 8.00 a.m. to 12 noon.

questions.q: Where would you go if you were collecting score cards?
questions.tip: Read across the score cards row to the 'Where' column.

questions.q: How many jobs may one pupil sign up for?
questions.tip: One word in the first paragraph is in bold for this reason.

questions.q: What must a helper wear?
questions.tip: The box at the bottom says what to wear. The badge is something you are given, not something you wear to start with.

questions.q: A pupil has a music lesson until 10.30 a.m. on Sports Day. Which job could she still do in full?
questions.tip: Find the only job that begins after 10.30 a.m.

visualTexts.title: How We Get to School
visualTexts.html:
HOW PRIMARY 3 GETS TO SCHOOL

All 120 Primary 3 pupils were asked one question: How did you come to school today? Each pupil chose one answer.

School bus
44 pupils
Car
31 pupils
Walk
25 pupils
Public bus
14 pupils
Bicycle
6 pupils

The survey was done on Monday, 6 October, which was a dry day.

questions.q: How many pupils were asked?
questions.tip: The sentence above the chart gives the total.

questions.q: Which way of coming to school was the most common?
questions.tip: Look for the longest bar.

questions.q: How many pupils came by car?
questions.tip: Read the number at the end of the 'Car' bar.

questions.q: How many more pupils took the school bus than walked?
questions.tip: Take the smaller number away from the larger one: 44 and 25.

questions.q: Which two ways together were chosen by 20 pupils?
questions.tip: Try adding the two smallest bars.

questions.q: How many pupils did NOT come by school bus?
questions.tip: Take the school bus number away from the total of 120.

questions.q: Why does the notice say the survey day was dry?
options: To explain why nobody was late
Because rain might have changed how pupils travelled
To show it was a Monday
Because the bicycle shed was closed
questions.tip: Think about what you would do differently on a wet morning.

questions.q: Which statement is true according to the chart?
options: More pupils walked than came by car
Half the pupils took the school bus
questions.tip: Check each statement against the numbers. Six is fewer than ten.

visualTexts.title: After-School Clubs, Term 4
visualTexts.html:
AFTER-SCHOOL CLUBS · TERM 4

Clubs run for eight weeks from 14 October. Each pupil may join two clubs, but not two on the same day.

ClubDayTimeOpen toFee
ChessMonday2.30 – 4.00 p.m.P3 to P6$16
ChoirTuesday2.30 – 3.30 p.m.P4 to P6Free
GardeningTuesday3.00 – 4.30 p.m.P3 to P5$8
RoboticsWednesday2.30 – 4.30 p.m.P5 and P6$40
ArtThursday2.30 – 4.00 p.m.P3 to P6$24
BadmintonThursday3.30 – 5.00 p.m.P4 to P6$12

Fees are for the whole term and are not refunded after the second session. Pupils on financial assistance pay nothing. Forms are due by 10 October.

questions.q: For how many weeks do the clubs run?
questions.tip: The sentence above the table gives the length of the term.

questions.q: Which club is free for everybody?
questions.tip: Look down the 'Fee' column.

questions.q: A Primary 4 pupil wants to join Robotics. Can she?
options: No, it is only for P5 and P6
Only if she joins Choir too
questions.tip: Check the 'Open to' column for Robotics.

questions.q: Which club finishes the latest?
questions.tip: Compare the finishing times, not the starting times.

questions.q: Why can a pupil not join both Choir and Gardening?
options: Gardening is not open to P6
The fees are too high together
questions.tip: Read the rule in the second sentence, then compare the two days.

questions.q: A Primary 4 pupil joins Art and Badminton. How much must he pay?
questions.tip: Add the two fees together — but first check whether both clubs are open to P4.

questions.q: A pupil leaves a club after the fourth session. What happens to her fee?
questions.tip: The box at the bottom explains when a refund is no longer possible.

questions.q: A Primary 3 pupil wants two clubs on different days and cannot pay any fees, and is not on financial assistance. Which pair could she choose?
options: None of the clubs would suit her
questions.tip: Work through the three conditions in turn: P3, two different days, and no fee. Only one club open to P3 is free — check whether there is one at all.

The library is choosing one app for Primary 3 and 4. Here is what each one offers.

BookNestReadAlong
Books for P3–P49001,400
Books read aloud to youAll of themAbout half
Works without internetYesNo
Cost for the school, one year$1,200$750

What 200 pupils said they wanted most

Read aloud
78 pupils
More books
56 pupils

A third of the school's tablets cannot connect to the internet outside the library.

questions.q: How many books for P3 and P4 does ReadAlong have?
questions.tip: Read across the first row to the ReadAlong column.

questions.q: Which app is cheaper for the school?
questions.tip: Compare the two figures in the 'Cost' row.

questions.q: What did most pupils say they wanted?
options: An app that works without internet
questions.tip: Look for the longest bar in the chart.

questions.q: Which app would suit a pupil with no internet at home?
questions.tip: Find the 'Works without internet' row.

questions.q: Which app gives teachers a record of what pupils have read?
questions.tip: The second-to-last row of the table answers this.

questions.q: How much more would BookNest cost the school in one year?
questions.tip: Take $750 away from $1,200.

questions.q: Why does the notice mention the school's tablets at the end?
options: To show the school has many tablets
Because an app needing internet would be unusable on some of them
To explain why the library is busy
Because tablets are expensive to repair
questions.tip: Match that last sentence with the 'Works without internet' row.

questions.q: Which app matches what pupils said they wanted most, AND works on every tablet?
questions.tip: Two conditions: the top bar in the chart, and the internet row. Check both against each column.
